# Overview

The MRM empirical callables (`mrm_otis_*`, `mrm_tps_*`,
`mrm_siu_*`) operate on three external data sources. This vignette
documents how rmorie makes each of them accessible:

* **OTIS** (Offender Tracking Information System; published by the
  Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General) -- public CKAN
  release on `data.ontario.ca`, reached via the existing
  `morie_load_dataset()` infrastructure.
* **TPS** (Toronto Police Service) -- public ArcGIS Open Data, reached
  via `morie_fetch_tps()`.
* **SIU** (Ontario Special Investigations Unit) -- public Director's
  Reports. `morie_fetch_siu()` writes the panel-reviewed corpus
  bundled in rmoriedata, or fetches the reports live on request.

Four small reference tables, read by `morie_sample()`, let the
examples run offline.

```{r intro}
library(rmorie)
```

# Included reference samples

`otis_b09` and `otis_c11` ship in rmorie and are the whole published
tables. `otis_b01` and `tps_assault` ship in rmoriedata and are
1,000-row extracts.

```{r samples}
# Included samples
b01 <- morie_sample("otis_b01")
b09 <- morie_sample("otis_b09")
c11 <- morie_sample("otis_c11")
tps <- morie_sample("tps_assault")

# Schema sanity
str(b01, max.level = 1)
nrow(b09)
nrow(c11)
dim(tps)
```

# OTIS via CKAN (`data.ontario.ca`)

The OTIS public release is hosted at
`data.ontario.ca/dataset/data-on-inmates-in-ontario` (31 resources
when this vignette was written, 29 of them CSV). The catalogue
registers these tables with their CKAN resource IDs:

```{r otis-keys}
catalog <- morie_dataset_catalog()
catalog[catalog$source == "otis", c("key", "name", "ckan_resource_id")]
```

To pull the full b01 from CKAN (network; not run when the vignette is
built):

```{r otis-load, eval = FALSE}
b01_full <- morie_load_dataset("otisb01")
nrow(b01_full)
# 82001 (October 2026)
```

The loader downloads the CSV on the first call, keeps it in the
per-user cache under `morie_cache_dir()`, and reads that copy on
later calls (`refresh = TRUE` downloads it again).

# TPS via ArcGIS Open Data

Toronto Police Service publishes per-category crime events through
ArcGIS Online. MORIE knows the layer URLs for nine categories.

```{r tps-urls}
morie_tps_layer_urls()
```

To fetch a single category (network; not run when the vignette is
built):

```{r tps-fetch, eval = FALSE}
csv_path <- morie_fetch_tps("Assault")
assault <- utils::read.csv(csv_path)
nrow(assault)
# 267796 (the layer count in October 2026)
```

The fetcher pages through `/query` with up to 2,000 records per page
(`max_per_page`) and writes `tps_Assault.csv` into `cache_dir`, which
defaults to a directory under `tempdir()`. Later calls in the session
return the cached path unless `overwrite = TRUE`; pass a persistent
`cache_dir` to keep the file between sessions.

Filtering at the server side:

```{r tps-filter, eval = FALSE}
recent <- morie_fetch_tps("Homicides",
                          where = "OCC_YEAR >= 2024",
                          overwrite = TRUE)
```

# SIU Director's Reports

The Ontario SIU publishes Director's Reports at `siu.on.ca`.
`morie_fetch_siu()` returns the path of an SIU.csv file. By default it
writes the panel-reviewed corpus bundled in rmoriedata, which needs no
network access:

```{r siu}
csv_path <- morie_fetch_siu(lang = "en")
siu <- utils::read.csv(csv_path)
dim(siu)
```

With `options(morie.siu.allow_fetch = TRUE)` it fetches the reports
live instead: it walks the DRID manifest shipped with rmorie
(`morie_siu_index()`), requests each report and news release at
`rate_rps` requests per second with `concurrency` parallel requests,
and parses them with the package's C++ parser. That takes a long time
and needs the network, so it is not run here:

```{r siu-live, eval = FALSE}
options(morie.siu.allow_fetch = TRUE)
csv_path <- morie_fetch_siu(lang = "en", cache_html = TRUE,
                            rate_rps = 4, overwrite = TRUE)
```

The `siu-pipeline` vignette covers the manifest, auditing and
corrections.

# Workflow: from included sample to verified result

Putting it together -- a complete worked example without any network
call:

```{r workflow}
b01 <- morie_sample("otis_b01")

# Mandela classification, one row per placement
mrm_classify_mandela(b01, denominator = "row")

# Segregation duration KM
mrm_otis_seg_duration_km(b01,
                         group_cols = "MentalHealth_Alert")

# Mortification co-occurrence: Cramer's V across alert pairs
mrm_otis_mortification_cooccurrence(b01)
```

For a full-data version, swap `morie_sample("otis_b01")` for
`morie_load_dataset("otisb01")` and re-run the same callables.

# Canadian case law and legislation via A2AJ and CanLII

Access to Algorithmic Justice (A2AJ) publishes Canadian court and
tribunal decisions and statutes and regulations as open data, through
a REST API and as one Parquet file per court on Hugging Face. The
`morie_ingest_a2aj_*` functions wrap both channels. The chunks in this
section need the network and are not run when the vignette is built.

```{r a2aj-coverage, eval = FALSE}
cov <- morie_ingest_a2aj_coverage("cases")
cov[cov$dataset %in% c("SCC", "ONCA", "FC"),
    c("dataset", "earliest_document_date", "number_of_documents")]
```

Search is full-text or by name, capped at 50 hits per call, and a
single decision comes back with its unofficial text:

```{r a2aj-search, eval = FALSE}
hits <- morie_ingest_a2aj_search("right to housing",
                                 dataset = c("SCC", "ONCA"),
                                 start_date = "2020-01-01")
doc <- morie_ingest_a2aj_fetch("2023 SCC 17", include_citations = TRUE)
substr(doc$unofficial_text_en, 1, 300)
doc$cases_cited_en[[1]]
```

For a whole court, load its Parquet file. The native reader decodes
the `LIST`-typed citation columns without `arrow`; pass `columns` to
skip the full texts, which dominate the file:

```{r a2aj-load, eval = FALSE}
sct <- morie_ingest_a2aj_load("SCT",
  columns = c("citation_en", "document_date_en", "cases_cited_en"))
edges <- morie_ingest_a2aj_citation_edges(sct)
head(sort(table(edges$to), decreasing = TRUE))
```

A2AJ does not yet carry the Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario, the BC
Human Rights Tribunal, the Ontario Superior Court, Alberta, Quebec or
the remaining provinces (its issues #1, #3 and #4), and individual
decisions can be missing (`2007 BCSC 1700`, issue #2). Those are
reachable through CanLII's API, which needs a free key
(`CANLII_API_KEY`; the chunk stops with a message without one) and
returns metadata plus the citation network rather than full text:

```{r canlii, eval = FALSE}
morie_ingest_a2aj_gaps()[, c("code", "canlii_database_id")]
hrto <- morie_ingest_canlii_cases("onhrt", result_count = 200,
                                  decision_date_after = "2024-01-01")
ids <- morie_ingest_canlii_case_id("2007 BCSC 1700")
morie_ingest_canlii_case(ids$database_id, ids$case_id)
```

Every A2AJ record carries an `upstream_license` field; check it before
any commercial use, and treat all texts as unofficial copies.

# Caching layout

| Data | Fetched by | Cached in |
|---|---|---|
| catalogue datasets (OTIS, PUMFs, ...) | `morie_load_dataset()` | per-user cache under `morie_cache_dir()` |
| TPS layers | `morie_fetch_tps()` | `cache_dir` argument (default under `tempdir()`) |
| SIU reports | `morie_fetch_siu()` | `cache_dir` argument (default under `tempdir()`) |
